12.t: Working with data: how much things expand
q: How much more did copper expand than steel?
A bimetallic strip is made of copper and steel. Use the data to predict which way it bends when heated.
Copper expands more than steel, so the strip bends with copper on the outside of the curve (towards the steel side).
A 100 m steel bridge warms by 50 degrees C. Estimate how much it expands, and explain why engineers leave gaps.
Steel: 6 mm per 10 m, so about 60 mm (6 cm) for 100 m. Without gaps the bridge would push against its ends and bend or crack; expansion joints let it grow and shrink safely.
